formation.value: Acts of Union 1800 united Great Britain and Ireland from 1 January 1801.

government.note: Parliamentary system; cabinet responsible to the Commons.

heir.note: Heir presumptive; Salic law separates Hanover on her accession.

power_groups.name: Whigs (with Radical and Irish allies, Lichfield House compact 1835)

laws.note: Mapping to game law categories is interpretive: Corn Laws (1815-1846) and Navigation Acts (to 1849) => protectionism; newspaper stamp duty ('taxes on knowledge') => limited press; state grants to voluntary schools since 1833 => religious schools; slavery abolished from 1 Aug 1834 (apprenticeship to 1838).

reforms.name: Representation of the People Act (Great Reform Act)

claims.basis: Joint occupation conventions with the USA (1818, renewed 1827)

territory.overseas_note: Colonies modelled as GBR regions: BNA, Caribbean, Guiana, Belize, Cape, Sierra Leone, Gambia, Mauritius, Ceylon, Australian colonies, Malta. Gibraltar, Heligoland, Bermuda, St Helena, Falklands are not modelled (gap).

structure.value: Most industrialised economy: mechanised cotton textiles, coal, iron, engineering; commercial agriculture; global shipping and finance.

tax_system.value: Customs and excise dominant; no income tax between 1816 and 1842.

crises.name: Great Famine in Ireland
crises.note: future; exogenous potato blight + system response

literacy.method: Signature rates in English marriage registers c. 1840 (men ~2/3, women ~1/2); Scotland higher, Ireland lower. Source to be attached.

society.religion_note: Established Church of England / Church of Ireland / Church of Scotland; Catholic Emancipation 1829; Irish Catholic majority.

foreign_policy.value: Palmerston (Foreign Secretary 1835-41): balance of power, support for liberal constitutional regimes (Quadruple Alliance 1834), Ottoman integrity against Russia, suppression of the slave trade, expansion of commerce.

rivals.basis: Eastern Question and Central Asia; Treaty of Hünkar İskelesi (1833)

diplomacy.relations_method: Ordinal judgement from Schroeder (1994) on alignments in 1834-36, mapped to a -100..100 scale; not a measured quantity.

army_personnel.note: Excludes the East India Company's armies.

navy.value: Largest navy in the world; numerous ships of the line in commission and in ordinary.

doctrine.value: Small long-service volunteer army officered by purchase; global naval supremacy; colonial garrisons.

railways_km.note: Series value for 1836 not checked; range reflects 1835-1840 growth.

strategic_priorities.rationale: Two-power naval standard as constant policy.
Keep Russia from the Straits; supported the Porte in 1839-41 and 1853-56.
Eastern Question and the defence of India.
Oriental Crisis: Convention of London (1840) forced Muhammad Ali out of Syria.
Canton system and the opium dispute led to the First (1839-42) and Second (1856-60) Opium Wars.
Peel's tariff reforms, Corn Law repeal (1846), Navigation Acts repeal (1849).
South Australia (1836), Port Phillip, New Zealand (1840).
Joint occupation, settled by partition in 1846 (Oregon Treaty).

historical_ai.notes: Priorities bias the shared AI's utilities; none are executed automatically.

personality.rationale: Derived from the 1836 profile: maritime commercial empire, gradual parliamentary reform, limited appetite for continental land war. Used in BOTH modes.
